title: Bugle, borrowed trumpet and first Italian wedding gig
summary: He learned bugle calls with the Woodcraft kids, got a trumpet, and sat in badly at an Italian wedding with Freddie Burns's band.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Oh. So, but then, no, it just happened to be in me. I'll tell you. I'll tell you. It was a, when I was working for the Western Union, I joined the Woodmen of the World. The kids, you know. Woodcraft, that's what it was. And then, I said, we need a bugle. So, a policeman out there by the name of Ben McKee. He said, well, I'll get you a bugle if you can play one. I said, well, I'll try it. So, he got me a bugle. And then, I practiced up on it and got a few bugle calls. And that was it. I could play the calls. And next thing you know, he says, well, no, I, a friend of mine brought a coronet, Frank Mead. They're a pretty well-known family in Orleans. Frank and Jim Mead. Frank had a, a, a trumpet. I wanted my old man to make a case for it. An old brass trumpet. So, I'd sneak the thing out, see. Fool around, you know, in the good old summertime and this, that and the other. But it's all about here. So, there was another fellow lived back of us. Freddie Burns. He played a car on that. And Freddie heard me playing one day. He came over and said, hey, I didn't know you could play any. Oh, I don't play. Hi, you want to play a day-go wedding with us? I said, what do you mean, me? Yeah, I said, get a book and a half and all you can eat and drink. I said, well, that ain't bad. It's Saturday night. So, Jesus, we go over there and I knew about five tunes I could remember. And Freddie played clarinet, his brother Charlie played bass, and you and Murray played guitar, and I played trumpet. Didn't have any drums. Little house in the house there. And they swung around there, rapping about the third tune. And the guy getting married said, hey, you want to dance? I was that bad, see? I followed up the whole deal. Oh, really?
You were that bad? Freddie didn't want to tell me I was bad. Yeah.
So, I said, yeah, I don't mind dancing. So, I danced and the first thing, you know, they played along and slow without me. The band sounded good.

Yeah. Well, they played together, see? I'd never play with them. So, little by little, the first thing, you know, I kept one. Freddie says, well, you learn some tunes. So, about a month later, you come over again. By this time, I'd had the whole repertoire on. Everything popular. I could whistle, and when I could whistle, I could play.
